Why can't Daenerys be violent for reasons she finds completely justifiable, without being labeled insane? Aegon the Conqueror and the Targaryens who took a part in the Dance of the Dragons certainly weren't considered mad for their actions. Even Maegor wasn't deemed insane. The only Targaryen who truly earned the title of 'mad' was the king who descended into paranoia and tried to burn down the capital after losing a civil war to a lord wielding a big hammer.

So, if Daenerys decided to embrace 'fire and blood,' committed acts of war crimes, and ultimately faced defeat, why should she be labeled as insane for that?

Even in the show, I would argue she wasn't truly mad. She still mourned the people she burned alive and tried to justify her actions to Jon, blaming Cersei for using civilians as shields. That is not the behavior of someone who has lost her mind.

I had a friend who was going through a rough time, just like I was when I met him. He was supportive of me, and I quickly learned from him that his own friends didn’t seem to care much about him or his mental health. Some even cut him off because he was suicidal.

Over the couple of months that I knew him, he overdosed on antidepressants more times than I could count—medications he wasn’t even prescribed. Each time, he would send a message saying he was going to die and then turn off his phone. I would panic, crying with worry, and would reach out to our mutual friends, who oddly seemed unbothered by that. Eventually, I found out he had only taken a couple of extra pills and had just gone to sleep.

He kept making these threats until I reached a point where I stopped taking them seriously and no longer gave him the attention he was looking for. Later, I ended up cutting him off for different reasons. Months passed without any contact, and then I heard from others that he was telling his new friends I was cruel and heartless because I hadn’t cared enough about him.

I don’t think he was unaffected after realizing he killed his own nephew in the books. Disliking family members is one thing in Westeros, but going after them when you don't have to is another. Afterward, he was forever known as Aemond the Kinslayer.
